text.fusion_control: A fusion control whose features come from a sarcasm model trained on permuted labels scores 0.648 ± 0.005; real vs. control features: no reliable difference (Δ = -0.001, 95% CI [-0.019, +0.016]). Any fusion effect is therefore not attributable to sarcasm knowledge.
text.full_ft: A diagnostic run with the token-embedding table unfrozen could not be completed: two attempts (batch 32, and batch 16 with 2-step gradient accumulation) drove the 16 GB machine to critical memory pressure and were stopped. Whether freezing contributes to the gap therefore remains open.
text.abstract_sarcasm: Multitask sarcasm supervision shows no reliable difference from the base model (Δ macro-F1 = +0.006, 95% CI [-0.014, +0.026]), and a shuffled-label control performs as well as real sarcasm labels (Δ = -0.002), so the sarcasm labels themselves add nothing measurable. Feature fusion with a separately trained sarcasm model shows no reliable difference from the base model (Δ = +0.007, 95% CI [-0.013, +0.026]). A Hinglish-pretrained encoder (HingRoBERTa) is the only transformer that approaches the TF-IDF baselines.
text.abstract_xai: deleting the top-attributed word lowers the predicted-class probability by 0.421 vs. 0.092 for a random word
text.abstract_early: flags toxic conversations with alarm F1 0.913 at a 0.051 false-alarm rate, but almost always at the first toxic turn rather than before it.
